basis: Inherited epidermal acantholysis causes recurrent erosions; despite its pemphigus synonyms, this is not autoimmune disease.
Immune immunoglobulin deposits damage glomeruli; associated lymphoproliferative disorders are separate diseases.
Polysyndactyly defines the syndrome; developmental delay 14/45 (~31%) and callosal hypoplasia 4/12 support neurologic involvement; single-case eye/heart findings excluded.
Cerebellar and motor-neuron degeneration; amyotrophy is neurogenic, and supranuclear ophthalmoplegia does not establish intrinsic eye disease.
Woolly hair and hypotrichosis define a hair disorder; protruding ears and everted lip alone do not establish functional organ damage.
Patellar aplasia and microtia define syndrome; speech delay 2/3 (~67%); airway malacia/emphysema 1/3 (~33%). Estimates are based on very few patients.
Adrenal aldosterone excess and hypokalemia with defining early severe hypertension; ventricular hypertrophy and hemorrhage are minority complications.
Malignancy originates in the male urethra, which belongs to the urinary axis.
Severe skeletal defects and defining cleft palate; CNS and cardiac malformations each 30–79%. Microtia omitted under cap; renal anomalies 5–29%.
Inflammation affects glans and preputial skin; infectious and noninfectious causes occur, so an infectious mechanism is not universal.
Growth hormone-secreting pituitary adenoma; pituitary origin is endocrine. No common direct damage to another organ is established.
Cardiac defects, skin disease and intellectual disability define CFC; visual abnormalities 80–99%, strabismus/ptosis 30–79%; skeletal findings omitted under cap.
Benign Schwann-cell neoplasm arising from peripheral nerve sheaths; cellular morphology does not establish another organ site.
Destructive nasal/sinus lesion, predominantly NK/T-cell lymphoma; palatal destruction is part of the defining lesion and supports gastrointestinal involvement.
Structural diverticula of the small intestine; no other organ involvement is established.
Immune-mediated injury to peripheral motor axons; weakness and possible ventilatory failure do not establish primary muscle or lung damage.
Phytanic acid metabolism disorder; retinopathy nearly universal, neuropathy/anosmia >70%, hearing loss ~60%; cardiac disease is less common.
Primary familial brain calcification affects basal ganglia; no systemic calcium disorder or other common organ damage is established.
Congenital splitting of the spinal cord within a single dural sac.
Inherited atrial arrhythmia and infra-Hisian conduction disease, with variable cardiomyopathy, are confined to the cardiac axis.
Adipocytic soft-tissue sarcoma typically arising in deep extremity soft tissues; no additional organ site is intrinsic to this histologic subtype.
Progressive neurodegeneration; photosensitive skin disease and sensorineural hearing loss each 4/4. Telangiectasia and photophobia alone do not establish ocular damage.
Isolated developmental eye malformation, including microphthalmia/anophthalmia and associated ocular structural defects.
Congenital myopathy with defining Robin/oral anomalies; ptosis 6/8 (~75%). Facial weakness is myopathic; developmental delay is occasional; hearing data are single-case.
Intellectual disability/spasticity, retinal dystrophy and diabetes insipidus define syndrome; sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in 30–79%.
